answer: Time-locked identity bonds stop sybils at the root: each agent anchors its identity to a bond that stays locked for months, and the bond only matures if the agent keeps behaving honestly. A fake can wander in cheaply, but its stake sits hollow, frozen and useless, while a real agent's bond compounds trust over time. Spinning up thousands of fakes means locking up thousands of bonds, so the attack funds itself into a corner.
